claims.text: High configurational entropy creates intrinsic local lattice distortions in high-entropy alloys.
Local lattice distortions transiently pin dislocations during dynamic loading.
Transient dislocation pinning increases HEA yield strength at lower-to-moderate dynamic strain rates.
At higher strain rates, applied stress overcomes lattice-distortion pinning and causes rapid dislocation de-pinning.
High-rate dislocation de-pinning sustains plastic deformation and preserves ductility.
Plastic deformation in the relevant HEAs is mediated by dislocation motion.
The proposed pinning-to-de-pinning behavior is more pronounced in HEAs than in lower-entropy alloys having similar baseline microstructures.
Relative to the baseline alloy, the HEA will have higher yield strength.
The HEA yield strength will increase with strain rate because of transient dislocation pinning.
The HEA will have greater strain-rate sensitivity of yield strength than the baseline alloy.
Dislocation de-pinning events will be observable at higher strain rates in the HEA.
The hypothesis should hold in single-phase HEAs from approximately 10^-4 to 10^2 s^-1.
The hypothesis should hold from room temperature to approximately 873 K.
Applicability of the mechanism to multiphase HEAs is uncertain.
The baseline can be made lower in configurational entropy and local lattice distortion while retaining a microstructure and processing history comparable to the HEA.
The quantitative yield-strength increase and the strain-rate threshold for de-pinning depend on HEA composition.
Failure to observe both enhanced strain-rate-dependent yield strength and the proposed pinning/de-pinning sequence relative to the baseline would falsify the hypothesis.
